description: Expert-curated directed causal graph for ROOTCAUSE. Nodes are environmental variables; edges are documented directional relationships with a source citation, an effect direction, and an optional condition under which the edge holds. This is a validation layer built from literature, not a statistically discovered graph.

nodes.label: Soil organic carbon
nodes.description: Carbon stored in soil organic matter; a core indicator of soil health.

nodes.label: Soil microbial diversity
nodes.description: Diversity and abundance of bacteria, fungi, and other soil microbiota.

nodes.label: Soil aggregate structure
nodes.description: Stability of soil aggregates, affecting porosity and infiltration.

nodes.label: Plant-available nitrogen
nodes.description: Nitrogen in forms usable by crops.

nodes.label: Soil pH
nodes.description: Acidity/alkalinity of soil.

nodes.label: Earthworm abundance
nodes.description: Population of earthworms, a soil bioindicator and ecosystem engineer.

nodes.label: Soil erosion rate
nodes.description: Rate of topsoil loss to wind and water.

nodes.label: Soil moisture retention
nodes.description: Capacity of soil to retain plant-available water.

nodes.label: Soil salinity
nodes.description: Salt concentration in soil, restricting plant water uptake.

nodes.label: Land use intensity (monoculture)
nodes.description: Degree to which land is under intensive, low-diversity cultivation.

nodes.label: Cover crop adoption
nodes.description: Use of non-cash crops planted to cover soil between main crop cycles.

nodes.label: Agroforestry adoption
nodes.description: Integration of trees and shrubs into cropland or pasture systems.

nodes.label: Deforestation rate
nodes.description: Rate of forest cover loss.

nodes.label: Tillage intensity
nodes.description: Degree of mechanical soil disturbance from ploughing.

nodes.label: Crop diversity
nodes.description: Number and variety of crop species grown in a system.

nodes.label: Grazing intensity (overgrazing)
nodes.description: Livestock grazing pressure relative to land carrying capacity.

nodes.label: Wetland extent
nodes.description: Area of natural wetland habitat.

nodes.label: Ground vegetation cover
nodes.description: Proportion of ground covered by living vegetation.

nodes.label: Pollinator abundance
nodes.description: Population of bees and other pollinating insects.

nodes.label: Natural pest predator abundance
nodes.description: Population of organisms that naturally control crop pests.

nodes.label: Species richness
nodes.description: Number of distinct species present in an area.

nodes.label: Habitat connectivity
nodes.description: Degree to which natural habitat patches are connected across a landscape.

nodes.label: Bird diversity
nodes.description: Diversity of bird species, an indicator taxon for ecosystem health.

nodes.label: Rainfall level
nodes.description: Regional precipitation, typically measured as annual mean rainfall.

nodes.label: Temperature extremes
nodes.description: Frequency and severity of heat stress events.

nodes.label: Drought frequency
nodes.description: Frequency of prolonged low-rainfall periods.

nodes.label: Pesticide use
nodes.description: Application intensity of synthetic pesticides.

nodes.label: Synthetic fertilizer use
nodes.description: Application intensity of synthetic nitrogen/phosphorus fertilizer.

nodes.label: Irrigation water use
nodes.description: Volume of water applied through irrigation.

nodes.label: Land degradation
nodes.description: Composite decline in land productive capacity.

nodes.label: Crop yield
nodes.description: Harvested output per unit area.

nodes.label: Nutrient / pollution runoff
nodes.description: Nutrients and agrochemicals leaving farmland into water bodies.

edges.mechanism: Cover crop biomass and root exudates add organic matter and feed soil biota.
edges.condition: annual rainfall above roughly 400mm, or supplemental irrigation available
edges.citation: Poeplau & Don (2015), 'Carbon sequestration in agricultural soils via cultivation of cover crops', Agriculture, Ecosystems & Environment.

edges.mechanism: In water-limited systems, cover crop growth consumes soil moisture that would otherwise be available to the following cash crop, competing for a scarce resource during establishment.
edges.condition: semi-arid or arid climate, annual rainfall below roughly 400mm
edges.citation: Blanco-Canqui et al. (2015), 'Cover Crops and Ecosystem Services: Insights from Studies in Temperate Soils', Agronomy Journal; FAO Global Soil Partnership guidance on cover cropping in dryland systems.

edges.mechanism: Organic carbon is the primary energy source for soil microbial communities; higher SOC supports greater microbial biomass and diversity.
edges.citation: Lori et al. (2017), 'Organic farming enhances soil microbial abundance and activity: a meta-analysis and meta-regression', PLOS ONE; Tsiafouli et al. (2015), Global Change Biology.

edges.mechanism: Fungal hyphae and microbial exudates bind soil particles into stable aggregates.
edges.citation: Six, Bossuyt, Degryze & Denef (2004), 'A history of research on the link between (micro)aggregates, soil biota, and soil organic matter dynamics', Soil & Tillage Research.

edges.mechanism: Healthier soil biology supports more vigorous flowering plant communities, indirectly increasing forage resources for pollinators.
edges.condition: flowering habitat present within pollinator foraging range
edges.citation: IPBES (2016), Assessment Report on Pollinators, Pollination and Food Production, general synthesis chapters on soil-plant-pollinator linkages.

edges.mechanism: Tree canopy reduces evaporative loss and leaf litter increases infiltration, improving moisture retention especially in low-rainfall systems.
edges.citation: FAO (2017), Agroforestry for Landscape Restoration; Global Soil Partnership technical guidance.

edges.mechanism: Tree and shrub flowering plus structural habitat complexity provide forage and nesting resources for pollinators.
edges.citation: Klein et al. (2007), 'Importance of pollinators in changing landscapes for world crops', Proceedings of the Royal Society B.

edges.mechanism: Mechanical disturbance breaks aggregates and accelerates microbial oxidation of stored carbon.
edges.citation: FAO (2011), Conservation Agriculture guidance; Six et al. (2004).

edges.mechanism: Bare, disturbed soil after tillage is more susceptible to wind and water erosion.
edges.citation: FAO (2019), Soil Erosion: The Greatest Challenge to Sustainable Soil Management.

edges.mechanism: Erosion preferentially removes carbon-rich topsoil.
edges.citation: FAO Global Soil Partnership, Global Soil Organic Carbon Map technical report.

edges.mechanism: Monoculture systems by definition reduce the number of crop species grown.
edges.citation: FAO (2019), The State of the World's Biodiversity for Food and Agriculture.

edges.mechanism: Diverse crops provide varied flowering periods and forage resources across the season.
edges.citation: Klein et al. (2007); IPBES (2016) Pollinator Assessment.

edges.mechanism: Structural and resource diversity supports habitat for predatory and parasitoid insects.
edges.citation: Landis, Wratten & Gurr (2000), 'Habitat management to conserve natural enemies of arthropod pests in agriculture', Annual Review of Entomology.

edges.mechanism: Effective natural pest control reduces the perceived need for chemical intervention.
edges.citation: Landis, Wratten & Gurr (2000).

edges.mechanism: Insecticides cause direct mortality and sublethal effects on pollinators.
edges.citation: IPBES (2016) Pollinator Assessment, Chapter on drivers of pollinator decline.

edges.mechanism: Broad-spectrum pesticides harm non-target predatory and parasitoid insects.
edges.citation: IPBES (2016) Pollinator Assessment.

edges.mechanism: Repeated high-rate application of ammonium-based nitrogen fertilizer acidifies soil over time.
edges.condition: sustained high application rates over multiple seasons
edges.citation: FAO Global Soil Partnership, Soil Acidification guidance note.

edges.mechanism: Strongly acidic soils are physiologically unfavorable for most earthworm species.
edges.citation: Edwards & Bohlen (1996), Biology and Ecology of Earthworms.

edges.mechanism: Earthworm burrowing and casting create stable macropores and aggregates.
edges.citation: Edwards & Bohlen (1996).

edges.mechanism: Direct addition of plant-available nitrogen.
edges.citation: FAO Global Soil Partnership, Soil Fertility guidance.

edges.mechanism: Nitrogen is typically the most limiting nutrient for crop growth up to an optimal rate.
edges.condition: below the crop-specific optimal application threshold; effect reverses at excess rates
edges.citation: FAO Global Soil Partnership, Soil Fertility guidance.

edges.mechanism: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus not taken up by crops leach or run off into waterways.
edges.condition: application exceeds crop uptake capacity, or heavy rainfall follows application
edges.citation: FAO (2018), Water Pollution from Agriculture: A Global Review.

edges.mechanism: Nutrient loading causes eutrophication, reducing aquatic and wetland species diversity.
edges.citation: IPBES (2018), Land Degradation and Restoration Assessment.

edges.mechanism: Forest clearance fragments remaining habitat patches.
edges.citation: IPBES (2019), Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services.

edges.mechanism: Connected habitat allows larger viable populations and species movement, standard landscape ecology / island biogeography result.
edges.citation: IPBES (2019) Global Assessment.

edges.mechanism: Connected habitat supports a wider range of bird species with different territory and migration needs.
edges.citation: IPBES (2019) Global Assessment.

edges.mechanism: Loss of root systems and canopy cover removes protection against wind and water erosion.
edges.citation: FAO (2019), Soil Erosion report.

edges.mechanism: Reduced forest evapotranspiration weakens regional moisture recycling, lowering rainfall at landscape scale.
edges.condition: large-scale, sustained deforestation over years to decades; effect is regional, not local or immediate
edges.citation: IPCC AR6 Working Group I, Chapter on land-atmosphere feedbacks.

edges.mechanism: Livestock trampling compacts soil, reducing porosity and aggregate stability.
edges.condition: grazing pressure exceeds land carrying capacity (overgrazing)
edges.citation: FAO (2021), Rangeland and Pasture Management guidance.

edges.mechanism: Stable aggregates and porosity improve water infiltration and storage.
edges.citation: Six et al. (2004).

edges.mechanism: Overgrazing removes vegetation faster than it can regenerate.
edges.condition: grazing pressure exceeds land carrying capacity (overgrazing)
edges.citation: FAO (2021), Rangeland and Pasture Management guidance.

edges.mechanism: Ground cover intercepts rainfall energy and binds soil with roots.
edges.citation: FAO (2019), Soil Erosion report.

edges.mechanism: Wetlands are disproportionately biodiverse habitat relative to their area.
edges.citation: IPBES (2018), Land Degradation and Restoration Assessment.

edges.mechanism: Wetland vegetation and soils filter and retain nutrients before they reach open water.
edges.citation: FAO (2018), Water Pollution from Agriculture: A Global Review.

edges.mechanism: More frequent drought reduces the baseline water available to replenish soil moisture.
edges.citation: IPCC AR6 Working Group II, Chapter on food security and land.

edges.mechanism: Water stress during critical growth stages reduces yield.
edges.condition: without supplemental irrigation or drought-adapted varieties
edges.citation: IPCC AR6 Working Group II.

edges.mechanism: More rainfall supports greater plant biomass, up to a site-specific saturation point.
edges.condition: below waterlogging threshold for the local ecosystem
edges.citation: General agroecology / rangeland ecology literature synthesized in FAO Land and Water reports.

edges.mechanism: Heat stress increases pollinator mortality and disrupts foraging activity.
edges.citation: IPBES (2016) Pollinator Assessment.

edges.mechanism: Heat stress beyond crop-specific thermal thresholds reduces flowering success and grain fill.
edges.condition: temperature exceeds crop-specific thermal threshold during a sensitive growth stage
edges.citation: IPCC AR6 Working Group II.

edges.mechanism: Evaporation of irrigation water leaves dissolved salts behind in the root zone.
edges.condition: poor drainage, or arid/semi-arid climate with high evaporation
edges.citation: FAO Global Soil Partnership, Soil Salinization guidance.

edges.mechanism: Salinity impairs root water uptake through osmotic stress.
edges.citation: FAO Global Soil Partnership, Soil Salinization guidance.

edges.mechanism: High salt concentration is osmotically stressful for most soil microorganisms.
edges.citation: FAO Global Soil Partnership, Soil Salinization guidance.

edges.mechanism: Composite loss of soil fertility, structure, and water-holding capacity lowers productive potential.
edges.citation: IPBES (2018), Land Degradation and Restoration Assessment.

edges.mechanism: Degraded land supports fewer viable niches and less primary productivity.
edges.citation: IPBES (2018), Land Degradation and Restoration Assessment.

edges.mechanism: Diversified rotations reduce pest/disease buildup and maintain soil cover more consistently than monoculture.
edges.citation: FAO (2019), The State of the World's Biodiversity for Food and Agriculture.
